source_text: Οὗτος γάρ ἐστιν ὁ πλοῦτος πολλῶν χρημάτων τιμιώτερος. Αὕτη ἡ κληρονομία ἀγαθὴ, παρὰ πατρὸς εἰς παῖδας παραπεμπομένη. «Εἰς δὲ κτῆμα ὀρφανῶν μὴ εἰσ έλθῃς.» Καὶ, «Μὴ συνδείπνει ἀνδρὶ βασκάνῳ.» Εἴρη ται καὶ περὶ τῆς βασκανίας. Προσκείσθω δὲ εἰς πλείονα φυλακὴν τοῦ κακοῦ, ὅτι ἴδιόν τι πάθος ἐστὶ τοῦ διαβόλου ἡ βασκανία. Οὐ γὰρ εὐθὺς διάβολος ἐκτίσθη ὁ διάβολος, ἀλλ' ἀγγέλου ἐξουσίαν λαβὼν, κατεστράφη εἰς τὴν τοῦ δαίμονος φύσιν. Καὶ ἐγένετο πονηρὸς δαίμων ὁ ταύτῃ τῇ πονηρίᾳ χαρακτηρισθεὶς, καὶ ἀπαλλοτριωθεὶς τῆς πρὸς τὸν Θεὸν οἰκειότητος, ἀποστραφεὶς δὲ πρὸς τὸ μέρος τῆς ἀποστασίας, ἐπειδὴ εἶδε τὸν ἄνθρωπον μικρὸν μὲν ζῶον, παρὰ πᾶσαν δὲ τὴν κτίσιν τιμιώτερον. Πρεσβύτερος ὢν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου, εἶδεν, ὅτι τὰ νηκτὰ πάντα λόγῳ ἐδημιουργήθη. «Ἐξαγαγέτω» γὰρ, φησὶ, «τὰ ὕδατα ἑρπετὰ ψυχῶν ζωσῶν.» Λόγῳ ἐποίησε τὰ κήτη τὰ κατὰ τὸ πέλαγος τὸ Ἀτλαντικὸν ἐνδιαιτώμενα. Λόγῳ ἐποίησε τὰ χερσαῖα. Προστάγματι Θεοῦ εἰς τὸ εἶναι παρήχθη. Προστάγματι γέγονε τὰ τῶν ἐλεφάντων μεγέθη, τὰ τῶν καμήλων· ἵπποι, καὶ βόες, καὶ ὅσα μεγέθει διαφέροντα καὶ ἰσχύϊ ζῶα, κατὰ ἀγέλας ἐκτίσθη ἑνὶ προστάγματι· καὶ τὸ ἔτι θαυμασιώτερον, προστάγματι οὐρανὸς, προστάγματι ἥλιος, προστάγματι βοτάνη, προστάγματι ἡ τῶν ὑδάτων φύσις, ἥ τε ὑπὲρ τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν ἐστορεσμένη, καὶ ταῖς κοιλότησιν ἐκκεχυμένη, πάντα προστάγματι· ὁ δὲ ἄνθρωπος χερσὶ διεπλάσθη. Εἶδε τὴν περὶ τὸν ἄνθρωπον τιμὴν, ἐβάσκηνεν ὁ διάβολος. Εἶδεν, ὅτι ἡλίου προτιμότερος. Ὁ μὲν γὰρ προστάγματι εἰς τὸ εἶναι παρῆλθεν· ὁ δὲ χερσὶ Θεοῦ διεπλάσθη. Καὶ ὁ μὲν ἐκτίσθη διὰ τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἄνθρωπος δὲ διὰ Θεόν· ἄνθρωπος, ἵνα Θεὸς δοξασθῇ· ἥλιος, ἵνα ἀνθρώποις ὑπηρετῇ. Κατέμαθε τὴν περὶ τὸν ἄνθρωπον τιμήν. Εἶδεν, ὅτι πρώτη ἡ κτίσις, τελευταῖος δὲ ὁ ἄνθρωπος, ὅτι παρεσκεύασεν αὐτῷ ὥσπερ οἰκοδεσπότῃ οἶκον πεπληρωμένον. Οὐ γὰρ πρῶτον ἐποίησεν ἄνθρωπον, ἵνα μὴ πτωχὸς κτισθῇ ἀλλ' ἐποίησεν οὐρανὸν, σκέπην αὐτοφυῆ κτίσας, ὑπεστόρεσε τὴν γῆν, ἰσχυρὸν ἔδαφος τοῖς ποσὶ προετοιμάζων τοῖς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου. Θάλλειν αὐτὴν ἐποίησε βοτανῶν καὶ καρπῶν παντοίαις φοραῖς. Πάντα εὐτρεπῆ τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ· τὰ ὑποζύγια εὐτρεπίσθη κατὰ ἀγέλας· ἐκτίσθη ἡ κτίσις. Τὰ μὲν σύννομα παρεσκευάσθη· τὰ δὲ ἄγρια πρὸς γυμνασίαν τοῦ σώματος. Τὰ μὲν πόνῳ κτητὰ, ἵνα φιλητὰ γένηται· τὰ δὲ ἑτοίμως παρόντα, ἵνα αὐτόθεν τῇ κτίσει ὑπηρετῆται. Εἶδεν, ὅτι αὐτομάτως ἡ γῆ τὸν καρπὸν αὐτοῖς παρεσκεύασε. Πᾶσα ἡ κτίσις ἐξεδέχετο τοὺς ἀπολαύοντας, καὶ εἰς ἑστίασιν παρήχθη ὁ ἄνθρωπος. Εἶδεν, ὅτι οὐκ ἠρκέσθη ὁ φιλάνθρωπος Θεὸς τῇ τῆς γῆς ἀπολαύσει· ἀλλ' ἐξαίρετον ἐνδιαίτημα, τὸ ἴδιον ἐγκαλλώπισμα, τὸν ἄνθρωπον ἑαυ-τοῦ βουλόμενος, ἐκεῖ κατέστησεν ἐν τῷ παραδείσῳ. Ἐπονηρεύσατο ὁ διάβολος ὁρῶν πολλὴν ἀπόλαυσιν περιῤῥέουσαν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ, ἀγγέλους παιδαγωγοὺς παρεδρεύοντας αὐτῷ· Θεὸν ὁμόγλωσσον γενόμενον τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, διαλεγόμενον ἀπὸ ἰδίας φωνῆς, πανταχόθεν τὸν παῖδα τὸν νήπιον παιδευόμενον, ἵνα εἰς Θεοῦ ὁμοιότητα ἀναδράμῃ· ἐπειδὴ κατέμαθε τὸν ἄνθρωπον, ἐπειδὴ εἶδεν, ὅτι τὸ μικρὸν τοῦτο ζῶον πρὸς τὴν τῶν ἀγγέλων ὁμοτιμίαν ὁ Κύριος προεκαλεῖτο· διὰ τῆς ἀρετῆς ἀνάγων αὐτὸν, καὶ διὰ σωφροσύνης τῶν κατὰ τὸν βίον ἐπὶ τὴν τελείωσιν τῆς ψυχῆς.
thought_title: Envy belongs to the devil who envied man
orientation: The preacher continues his teaching on cures for the passions and turns to envy as the devil's own passion against honored man.
pass_a_gloss: For this is the wealth more honorable than much money. This inheritance is good, being handed over from father to children. But into property of orphans do not enter. And, Do not eat together with an envious man. It has been spoken also concerning envy. But let it be added for greater guard against the evil, that envy is a certain peculiar passion of the devil. For the devil was not created as devil straightway, but having received authority of an angel, he was overturned into the nature of a demon. And he became an evil demon, he who was marked by this evil, and was estranged from the closeness toward God, and turned away toward the side of revolt, because he saw man, a small living thing, yet more honorable than all creation. Being older than man, he saw that all the swimming things were created by word. For Bring forth, it says, let the waters bring forth creeping things of living souls. By word he made the sea monsters dwelling in the Atlantic sea. By word he made the land animals. By command of God it was brought into being. By command came to be the bulks of elephants, the bulks of camels; horses, and oxen, and as many living things as excel in bulk and in strength, were created in herds by one command; and what is still more wonderful, by command heaven, by command sun, by command plant, by command the nature of the waters, both that spread above heaven and earth and that poured out into the hollows, all by command; but man was molded by hands. He saw the honor concerning man, the devil envied. He saw that he was more preferred than sun. For the one came into being by command; but the other was molded by hands of God. And the one was created because of man, but man because of God; man, in order that God be glorified; sun, in order that it serve men. He learned the honor concerning man. He saw that creation was first, but man last, because He prepared for him as for a master of a house a house that was filled. For He did not make man first, in order that he not be created poor, but He made heaven, creating a roof grown of itself, He spread the earth beneath, preparing strong ground for the feet, the feet of man. He made it sprout with plants and fruits by all kinds of yieldings. All things were ready for man; the beasts of burden were made ready in herds; creation was created. The tame things were prepared as companions; but the wild things for training of the body. The things acquired by toil, in order that they become loved; but the things present at once, in order that he be served by creation immediately. He saw that the earth of its own accord prepared the fruit for them. All creation was awaiting those who would enjoy, and man was brought in for a feast. He saw that God who loves man was not content with enjoyment of the earth; but wishing man for himself as a choice dwelling, his own ornament, He settled him there in paradise. The devil became evil seeing much enjoyment flowing around man, angels as tutors sitting beside him; God become using the same tongue with men, conversing from his own voice, the child the infant being instructed from every side, in order that he run up to likeness of God; because he learned man, because he saw that the Lord was calling this small living thing to equal honor with the angels; leading it up through virtue, and through soundness of mind over the things in life to the perfection of the soul.

pass_b_english: For this is wealth, and it counts for more than a large sum of money. This is a good inheritance, handed down from a father to his children. Scripture says, "Do not encroach on the property of orphans" (Proverbs 23:10). And it says, "Do not share a meal with an envious man" (Proverbs 23:6). That word was spoken about envy.

Let me add this word, so you will guard more fully against this evil. Envy is a passion that belongs to the devil in a special way. The devil was not created a devil from the beginning. He had received the rank of an angel, and then he sank down into the nature of a demon. He became an evil demon, and this evil marked him. He lost his kinship with God, and he turned to the side of rebellion. He did this because he saw the human being. Man is a small creature, yet he ranks higher than all creation.

The devil is older than man. He saw that God made every swimming creature by a word. For God says, "Let the waters bring forth swarms of living creatures" (Genesis 1:20). By a word He made the whales that live in the Atlantic sea. By a word He made the land animals. By the command of God He brought them into being. By a command came the bulk of elephants and camels. Horses and oxen, and every animal that stands out for size and strength, He created in herds by a single command. Still more wonderful, heaven came by a command, and the sun by a command, and grass by a command. The whole nature of the waters came by a command, both the waters spread above heaven and earth, and the waters poured into the hollows. All things came by a command. But man was molded by hands. The devil saw the honor given to man, and he envied him.

He saw that man ranks higher than the sun. The sun came into being by a command, but man was molded by the hands of God. The sun was created for the sake of man, but man was created for the sake of God. Man exists so that God will be glorified, and the sun exists so that it will serve men. The devil recognized the honor given to man. He saw that creation came first and man came last. God had prepared a full house for him, as for a master of a house. God did not make man first, or man would have been created poor. He made heaven, and He built a roof that grew of itself. He spread out the earth below, and He prepared solid ground under the feet of man. He made the earth sprout grasses and fruits in every kind of abundance. Everything stood ready for man. The draft animals stood ready in herds. Creation was complete. The tame animals were prepared as companions, and the wild animals were prepared to exercise the body. Some animals come by toil, so men will love them. Others stand ready at hand, so men are served by creation at once. The devil saw that the earth prepared its fruit for men by itself. All creation waited for those who would enjoy it, and man was led in as a guest to a feast.

He saw that God, who loves mankind, was not content with the enjoyment of the earth. God wanted man for Himself, as His own special dwelling and His own ornament, and He set him there in paradise. The devil turned evil as he watched this rich enjoyment pouring around man — angels standing beside him as his tutors, God sharing the same tongue with men and speaking with them in His own voice, and the young child trained on every side, so he would run upward into the likeness of God — because he had taken man's measure, because he had seen that the Lord was calling this small creature to equal honor with the angels, leading him upward through virtue, and through self-control in the things of this life toward the perfection of the soul.

problems.quote: Angels stood beside man as his tutors. God used the same tongue with men, and He spoke with them in His own voice. On every side the young child was trained
problems.source_quote: ὁρῶν πολλὴν ἀπόλαυσιν περιῤῥέουσαν τῷ ἀνθρώπῳ, ἀγγέλους παιδαγωγοὺς παρεδρεύοντας αὐτῷ· Θεὸν ὁμόγλωσσον γενόμενον τοῖς ἀνθρώποις, διαλεγόμενον ἀπὸ ἰδίας φωνῆς, πανταχόθεν τὸν παῖδα τὸν νήπιον παιδευόμενον
problems.why: These are things the devil sees as he turns malicious; English states them as bare facts, and the following because-clauses lose their cause.
problems.fix: He saw rich enjoyment around man, angels attending him as tutors, God sharing man's tongue and speaking in His own voice, and the young child trained on every side so he might rise to God's likeness, because the devil had taken man's measure and had seen the Lord calling this small creature to equal honor with the angels.
problems.ruling: Participle ὁρῶν governs the accusatives (ἀγγέλους παρεδρεύοντας, Θεὸν γενόμενον, παῖδα παιδευόμενον); English states them as facts, and 'ἐπειδὴ κατέμαθε' causal link is lost.
